title: Property B_k: k-Colorability of Hypergraphs
description: Generalizes Property B (2-colorability) to Property B_k (k-colorability). Proves monotonicity in k, equivalence B ↔ B_2, and states the generalized first-moment threshold k^{t-1}/(k-1).

meta.author: Erdős (generalized)
meta.assumptions: No axioms. All theorems proved from Mathlib. The generalized first-moment bound is stated as a definition.

relatedProblems.relationship: Parent problem: Property B and sparse set families

overview.text: A formalization generalizing Property B (hypergraph 2-colorability) to Property B_k (k-colorability). Defines HasPropertyBK: there exists a k-coloring such that no set in the family is monochromatic. Proves 10 theorems: monotonicity in k (B_k → B_{k+1}), equivalence with the original Property B when k=2, singleton/empty family base cases, and the k-color hierarchy. States the generalized first-moment threshold as an open question.
overview.historicalContext: Property B was introduced by Bernstein (1908) for 2-colorings and studied extensively by Erdős and Hajnal. The k-color generalization relates to hypergraph chromatic number, connecting to list coloring and the Erdős-Faber-Lovász conjecture. The probabilistic threshold k^{t-1}/(k-1) generalizes Erdős's 2^{t-1} bound.
overview.problemStatement: Define Property $B_k$ for set families: does there exist a $k$-coloring of the ground set with no monochromatic member? Determine the threshold family size below which Property $B_k$ is guaranteed.
overview.proofStrategy: Property B_k is defined using colorings χ : α → Fin k. Monotonicity is proved by embedding Fin k → Fin (k+1) via castSucc. The equivalence B ↔ B_2 uses the bijection between 2-colorings and subsets S = χ⁻¹(0).
keyInsights: Property B_k is monotone in k: embedding k colors into k+1 colors preserves non-monochromaticity
Property B (Erdős #1022) is exactly Property B_2: the equivalence is proved via the correspondence between 2-colorings and set membership
The generalized first-moment threshold is k^{t-1}/(k-1), recovering 2^{t-1} when k=2
All theorems are axiom-free — the generalization adds no new assumptions beyond the parent formalization
prerequisites: Probability (first-moment method, for understanding the threshold)

sections.title: Core Definition
sections.summary: Defines HasPropertyBK: there exists χ : α → Fin k such that no nonempty member is monochromatic.

sections.title: Basic Properties
sections.summary: Empty family has B_k, B_k is hereditary, singleton families with ≥2-element sets have B_k.

sections.title: Monotonicity in k
sections.summary: Proves B_k → B_{k+1} via Fin.castSucc embedding, and the general version B_k → B_m for k ≤ m.
sections.mathContext: $B_k(F) \implies B_{k+1}(F)$ (embed $[k] \hookrightarrow [k+1]$). More generally, $k \leq m \implies B_k \implies B_m$.

sections.title: Connection to Property B
sections.summary: Proves B ↔ B_2 via the bijection between 2-colorings and subsets.
sections.mathContext: $B(F) \iff B_2(F)$ for families of nonempty sets.

sections.title: Generalized First-Moment Threshold
sections.summary: States the generalized bound: |F| < k^{t-1}/(k-1) with min size ≥ t implies B_k.

conclusion.summary: An axiom-free formalization of Property B_k extending Erdős #1022. The k-color hierarchy B_2 ⊆ B_3 ⊆ ... is proved, and the equivalence B = B_2 formally connects this to the parent problem. The generalized first-moment threshold provides the k-color analogue of Erdős's 2^{t-1} bound.
conclusion.implications: Understanding Property B_k for k > 2 connects to hypergraph chromatic number theory and the Erdős-Faber-Lovász conjecture (proved by Kang et al., 2023). The sparsity conjecture from Erdős #1022 could be strengthened to ask about k-colorability thresholds.
openQuestions: Does the sparsity conjecture (Erdős #1022) generalize to k-colorability with a threshold c(t,k) → ∞?
What is the chromatic threshold: the minimum k such that c(t)-sparse families of t-sets have Property B_k?
